proposals.observation: The Daily Blog Post workflow failed at 09:03 on 16 June. There is only one post queued against 47 published, meaning the pipeline that generates and queues new posts is not running. If this stays broken, the content queue empties within days and organic search traffic stops compounding. The Funnel-Hack Digest also failed the same day, but the blog post workflow is higher priority because content is the top-of-funnel for the quiz.
proposals.proposal: Open the Daily Blog Post workflow file and read the most recent failure logs (the sha history shows no remediation commit after 922a58d). The fix is almost certainly a changed secret name, an expired API key reference, or a Node version mismatch introduced without a corresponding workflow update. Patch whichever single line is throwing, commit with message "fix(ci): restore daily-blog-post workflow", and confirm the next scheduled run passes. Do not touch .github/workflows/* for any other workflow in the same edit to keep the blast radius small.
proposals.new_text:
# No copy replacement. This is a CI configuration fix.
# Locate the failing step in .github/workflows/daily-blog-post.yml.
# The most common causes given the repo pattern:
#   1. An env var renamed (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY vs OPENAI_KEY) — check the "env:" block.
#   2. Node version pinned to 18.x but actions/setup-node now defaults differently — pin explicitly: node-version: '20'.
#   3. A changed output path that no longer matches the glob in the publish step.
# Apply the single-line fix, commit, re-run manually to verify before next scheduled trigger.

proposals.observation: In the last 48 hours the quiz recorded one session that loaded the intro page and went no further. Zero starts, zero completions. One visitor saw the intro and left. That is a 0% start rate from a cold-direct visit, which means the intro screen is not doing enough work to earn the click into question one.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the intro-screen call-to-action copy. The current text (below) is generic enough that any financial coach could have written it. Replace it with copy that names the specific tension the ICP is sitting in right now: earning well, spending freely, but with nothing to show for it at month-end. Keep the Sultanic test in mind: the sentence must be something only Joel could write, referencing the lived reality of the money-script work he does.
proposals.current_text: Take our free quiz to discover your money personality and start your journey to better financial habits.
proposals.new_text:
You earn well. Most months, though, there is nothing left to prove it.

This quiz takes four minutes. It will show you the specific thought pattern that is quietly running your financial decisions — the one that was already there long before the salary went up.

Joel Grayson, MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner, built it from the same research framework he uses with clients who earn good money and still feel financially stuck.

Start the quiz.

proposals.impact: lifts 37.5% open rate toward the 66% seen on Money Vigilance sequence
proposals.observation: The Money Worship automation has a 37.5% open rate across 16 sends. The Money Vigilance sequence, which covers comparable emotional territory, is sitting at 66.67% on 12 sends. That is a 29-percentage-point gap. The most controllable variable in open rate is the subject line. Improving email one's subject line costs one file edit and could recover a meaningful share of those unopened sends before the sequence grows larger.
proposals.proposal: Replace the subject line of email one in the Money Worship sequence. The current line is benefit-generic. The Money Vigilance sequence likely outperforms because its subject lines are more specific to the tension the reader named when they completed the quiz. Rewrite the Money Worship subject line to name the exact bind: the reader ties their self-worth to their earning or spending, and they already suspect it.
